demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Sugar export business remained un-remunerative and un-competitive since the start of the new season owing to subdued global prices/demand, and the Middle East conflict halted shipping services to West Asia and Africa, badly impacting export business.
- The company timely developed and expanded domestic trade of Sugar and other Agri Commodities with pan-India spread, maintaining growth trajectory via an established supply chain of Maize to multigrain refineries for ethanol production.
- The company developed a robust supply chain business of bulk Sugar to Industrial & Institutional consumers, which has been growing at a fast pace.
- Domestic sugar sector experienced a significant uptick fuelled by India's restrictive export policies aimed at stabilizing local prices and managing food inflation; the company maintained market share domestically leveraging its supply chain and strategic positioning.
- Grains verticals (Maize & Soybean seed) saw profitable contributions but face challenges of price mismatches, sluggish demand, tight liquidity, and geopolitical uncertainties including trade tensions and tariff barriers.
- Indian exporters with scale, compliance mechanisms and consistent quality are gaining greater relevance as buyers diversify procurement into more resilient, multi-geography supply chains.
- India's core long-term growth drivers — strong domestic demand, structural reforms and a resilient economic foundation — remain intact despite near-term headwinds.

capex_expansion.body: The company is expanding its domestic footprint by establishing strategic depots for Sugar and other Agri Commodities with pan-India spread, and has grown its international presence by forming a new wholly-owned subsidiary, Sakuma Impex Ltd, in London (UK) during the year, alongside existing subsidiaries in the UAE and Singapore and step-down subsidiaries in Ghana and Tanzania.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Currency fluctuations are accentuated by global trade disputes and sanctions, which can impact profitability.
- Trade barriers and tariffs influence the international pricing landscape, requiring dynamic sourcing and pricing strategies.
- Due diligence and financial instruments such as letters of credit are crucial to navigate global trade complexities.
- Insured storage and transportation are needed to mitigate losses due to geopolitical conflicts, tariffs, and supply chain disruptions.
- Escalating tariffs, trade wars, quota limitations, export bans and non-tariff barriers in major economies threaten the free flow of commodities and restrict export volumes, raising costs and market uncertainty.
- Rising logistics and supply chain costs, driven by geopolitical tensions and disruptions, diminish margins.
- Unpredictable monsoon patterns and climate change threaten crop yields, impacting domestic supply and exports.
- Labour shortages, especially in agricultural sectors, are exacerbated by migration, border restrictions, and labor laws.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Recalibrated strategy to strengthen domestic trading networks by establishing depots in strategic regions and boosting sales of sugar, pulses and maize for ethanol, in response to global trade tensions.
- Investing in international trading capabilities to diversify supply sources and markets, mitigating tariff and quota risks.
- Focus shifted towards expanding domestic markets and diversifying into new commodities to sustain growth momentum, given export quota limitations, bans and non-tariff barriers.
- Acting as re-export partners leveraging relationships with international suppliers from Australia, Canada and other markets where trade barriers may affect market access.
- Expanded international footprint through subsidiaries (in the UK) to capitalize on global demand and maintain supply chain agility amidst geopolitical uncertainties.
- Proactive risk management including currency hedging, flexible contractual arrangements with suppliers and buyers, and cargo insurance coverage.
